title: Straight-Line Graphs Adventure
welcome_lead: Time to read graphs! You'll meet y = mx + c, plot lines from tables, and measure gradients.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Graphs — y = mx + c, plotting straight lines, and finding gradient as rise over run.
final_note: You can read off the gradient and intercept, plot a line from a table, and measure rise over run.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Every straight line has the equation y = mx + c.

m is the gradient (steepness). c is the y-intercept (where the line crosses the y-axis).

For y = 2x + 3: gradient is 2, y-intercept is 3. The line goes up 2 for every 1 across.

Pick values of x, work out y, plot the points, draw the line.

For y = 2x + 1: when x = 0, y = 1. When x = 1, y = 3. When x = 2, y = 5.

Plot (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5) — they line up. Join with a ruler.

Pick any two points on the line. Gradient = (change in y) / (change in x).

From (1, 3) to (4, 9): rise = 9 − 3 = 6, run = 4 − 1 = 3. Gradient = 6/3 = 2.

A negative gradient means the line goes down from left to right.
